task_name: Wiring gate 1 into the server it runs in

rubric.result: The objective promises three things and the diff produces all three. (a) 'the running backend serves /spec-freeze': api-server.ts mounts `app.get(SpecFreezeRoute.PATH, ...)`, `app.post(...)` and `app.all(SpecFreezeRoute.PATH, SpecFreezeRoute.refuseOtherMethods)`, and `ApiCollaborators` plus the constructor and the fields carry readSpecFreeze, freezeSpec and gateKey to them. (b) 'with the disk, the git and the gh this entrypoint already builds': ct-api.ts builds `new DiskEpicSpecs({ list: Disk.list, read: Disk.read, write: Disk.write })`, `new GitEpicBranch({ run: git })` on the launcher already created at line 402 (`const git = CtApi.#tool(GitWorkspace.BIN)`), and both use cases take the `pullRequests` (`new GhPullRequests({ gh })`, line 440) the entrypoint already had; the new `Disk.list` is what the DiskEpicSpecs port signature `ListNames = (path) => Promise<string[] | null>` needed. (c) 'make dev-frontend proxies it': `'/spec-freeze'` joins API_PATHS in frontend/vite.config.ts, which is what builds server.proxy. Nothing the objective names is missing.

The TDD line names two tests and both are in the diff with the assertions written down. First: `it('the_spec_freeze_read_is_served_and_another_method_on_its_path_is_refused')` in api-server.test.ts — the plan asks for 'a GET reaches the doubled query and a DELETE answers 405 with Allow: GET, POST', and the body asserts `expect(response.status).toBe(200)`, `toEqual({ status: 'no-spec' })`, `expect(readSpecFreeze.asked).toHaveLength(1)` (the doubled query was reached), `expect(refused.status).toBe(405)` and `expect(refused.headers.get('allow')).toBe('GET, POST')`. Second: `it('a_whole_request_to_spec_freeze_reaches_the_wiring_the_entrypoint_built')` in ct-api-real-process.test.ts — the amended line asks for the entrypoint started with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR on a mkdtemp directory answering `200 {"status":"none"}`, and the body is `Entrypoint.listening({ CT_API_PORT: '0', CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR: state })` with `expect(response.status).toBe(200)` and `toEqual({ status: 'none' })`. Same assertion, same input, same expected value in both.

The task carries no `Contract (path):` block; it carries a `Call site (backend/src/infrastructure/api-server.ts):` block and prose naming the symbols to build. The call site is reproduced verbatim, line for line, including `Browsers.turnAwayForeign` on both verbs, the argument order `(this.coordinatingSessions!, this.readSpecFreeze!, this.gateKey!)` / `(..., this.freezeSpec!, this.gateKey!)` and the `app.all` fallback. The prose-named symbols also match name by name: `ApiCollaborators` gains `readSpecFreeze?: ReadSpecFreeze | null`, `freezeSpec?: FreezeSpec | null`, `gateKey?: GateKey | null` (optional and nullable like every other one); `Disk.list(path)` returns `readdir`'s names and `null` on ENOENT, reusing the file's own `Disk.#isMissing`; `new GateKey({ random: randomBytes })`; `new ReadSpecFreeze({ specs, branch, pullRequests })` and `new FreezeSpec({ specs, branch, pullRequests, now: () => new Date() })` match the constructors declared in read-spec-freeze.ts and freeze-spec.ts.

Row by row, the rows this diff bears on are implemented with their stated value. D-10 ('everything new under backend/ is TypeScript'): every touched backend file is .ts and the additions use only erasable syntax. D-22 ('the gates are the human's'): both handlers are mounted behind `Browsers.turnAwayForeign` and receive the `gateKey`, and the vite proxy entry is exactly the mechanism the task describes — the proxy strips `Origin`, so under `make dev-frontend` the read mints no key. D-11 ('a yardstick is imported, never reimplemented'): the wiring builds no second opinion, it only injects the existing use cases. D-23 and D-7: nothing in this diff merges or writes to a pull request. D-13: nothing is stored; the state is still derived by ReadSpecFreeze. D-16 ('no module under backend/src names cmux'): the diff adds no cmux reference. Every other row is untouched by this diff and therefore complies.

Exemplars: `ReadSpecFreezeSpy` copies the file's own `StartPlanSpy` idiom exactly (extends the use case, `super(...)` with the bare ports, records what it was asked, overrides `execute`), and `CoordinatingSessionFixture.live()` follows the same shape as the `Mother.live()` of spec-freeze-route.test.ts without sharing a module — which is what `conventions/testing.md` prescribes ('What several test types of the same module share lives in a type they inherit from, not in a loose function and not in a shared module imported from one place only'); these are two different modules, so a fixture each is idiom, not a spread decision under `conventions/decisions.md`. Boundaries: `conventions/boundaries.md` says the outer edge 'is the only place that assembles the dependency graph: it picks the concrete adapters and injects them', and every adapter here (DiskEpicSpecs, GitEpicBranch, GateKey) is constructed in ct-api.ts and injected by name; the git launcher it reuses carries its cap (`ToolRunner({ bin, budgetMs })`), so no call leaves uncapped and no adapter picks its own. `conventions/architecture.md`: no new module is created, the three collaborators enter ApiServer through the constructor by name, and nothing new was placed inside an old file as a new concept — `Disk.list` genuinely extends the `Disk` namespace that already holds `read`, `write`, `exists`. `conventions/style.md`: no comment, no prose, English throughout, every function hangs off a type (`Disk.list` static, the spies' methods). `conventions/simplicity.md`: each of the three added fields has a caller today — readSpecFreeze and gateKey in `SpecFreezeRoute.reading`, freezeSpec and gateKey in `SpecFreezeRoute.freezing`. `backend/conventions/this-repository.md`: the suite convention 'every spawned child is killed in afterEach' holds — the new real-process test relies on `Entrypoint.killAll()` in `afterEach`, and it lives in the `-real-process` file, which is the marker `conventions/testing.md` asks for. `frontend/README.md` describes the proxy and its Origin stripping; the new path joins the same array and inherits both. The named skills were loaded: `backend-engineering:backend-best-practices` is a Python/Django router and, per this repository's own precedence list, yields to the travelling yardstick — nothing in it bears on this TypeScript wiring; `frontend-engineering:frontend-best-practices` quick rules (no semicolons, single quotes, UPPER_SNAKE_CASE config constant) are respected by the one-entry addition to API_PATHS. `conventions/defects.md`, rule by rule: (1) closed vocabulary — the diff introduces no classifier; the states it carries come from the pre-existing `SpecFreezeState` frozen object, and the test asserts the literal wire values rather than deriving a boolean; no dispatch and no catch-all is added. (2) raw map as the return value of logic — none: `Disk.list` answers `string[] | null`, the two use cases answer their declared result objects (`SpecFreezeRead`, `SpecFrozen`), and `ApiCollaborators` is a declared constructor parameters type, not a map returned by logic. (3) two fields that have to agree / sentinel — none: the absence of a directory is carried by `null` in the return type of `Disk.list` (the same idiom as the neighbouring `Disk.read`, and the shape `DiskEpicSpecs`' `ListNames` port declares), not by an empty array standing for 'missing'; the three new collaborators are independent and nothing has to agree with anything. (4) an error named for where it happens — no error type is added or renamed in this diff.

No subject. The two touched test files carry only `+` lines: api-server.test.ts grows imports, `ReadSpecFreezeSpy`, `CoordinatingSessionFixture` and one new `it`, and ct-api-real-process.test.ts grows one new `it`. The only `-` lines in the whole diff are outside test files — one import line in ct-api.ts, one constructor destructuring line in api-server.ts, the API_PATHS array in vite.config.ts and two prose lines of the plan — and none of them is an assertion, a case or a test.

The promised behaviour is produced by production code, not by scaffolding. Serving the path is `app.get/app.post/app.all(SpecFreezeRoute.PATH, ...)` in src/infrastructure/api-server.ts, and the collaborators behind it are built in src/infrastructure/ct-api.ts. Both tests would fall with those production lines reverted: without the mounts, `GET /spec-freeze` reaches `Failures.nothingMatched` and answers 404 instead of 200, in the test server and in the real spawned process alike. The real-process test in particular is answered by the graph the entrypoint assembled — no double exists in that process.

Inside the five declared files, every line traces to a sentence of the task: the three collaborators and the call site in api-server.ts, the `Disk.list` helper plus the five constructions and the three collaborator arguments in ct-api.ts (I read the whole surrounding of that long entrypoint — lines 110-182 and 398-575 — and nothing else in it moved: no reordering, no unrelated adapter, no extra import beyond `readdir`, DiskEpicSpecs, GitEpicBranch, GateKey, ReadSpecFreeze and FreezeSpec), the one entry in API_PATHS, and the two tests the `**Tests:**` line names. Nothing in `### Out of scope` is touched: no groom, no slices.js, no plugin skill, no merge, no write to a pull request, no change to start-plan/implement-plan/plan events/harvest/dispatcher. The sixth path is the plan hunk, an amendment, and I read it line by line: it rewrites two prose lines of THIS task's `**TDD:**` into three, adding that the entrypoint is started with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` on a `mkdtemp` directory and why. It removes no route from `**Files:**`, keeps both prescribed test names verbatim, keeps `**Tests:**` and all four `**Verification:**` commands untouched, and disarms no control — it makes a control stricter by demanding isolation the first attempt lacked. It is justified: `conventions/testing.md` refuses a suite that 'has to reach a service in order to have a case', and the un-amended line prescribed a test that read this machine's real recorded session and reached GitHub.

Two new tests, and both hold the three properties. Deterministic: no clock, no date, no randomness (the gate key's `random` is `(size) => Buffer.alloc(size, 1)`, fixed), no sleep, no fixed port (`port: 0` in the test server, `CT_API_PORT: '0'` in the spawned one), and no network — the real-process test's `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR: state` on a fresh `mkdtemp` is precisely what keeps `records.recall()` answering null (the state root is read from that variable in invocation.ts), so it never recovers a session, never reads a checkout's spec and never reaches `gh`. Isolated: each builds its own state — a fresh `CoordinatingSessions` per call, a fresh spy, a fresh temporary directory — the test server is stopped by `RunningApi.stopAll()` in `afterEach`, the spawned process is killed by `Entrypoint.killAll()` in `afterEach`, and the temporary directory is removed at the end, the way the two CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR tests above it already do; neither needs an order from the rest of the file. Verifies real behaviour: the assertions are the status and the literal body over a real listening server and a real client, which is the controller row of `conventions/testing.md`; `readSpecFreeze.asked` is asserted as what the doubled use case received, not as a mock's return value, and both tests fail if the mounts are removed. I loaded `control-tower-loop:test-driven-development` as instructed and found nothing in it, or in the anti-patterns it names, that the two tests contradict on a point the implementer could have decided: the one thing I would note — the first test's name joins two facts with 'and', which the skill's 'Minimal' row would split — is the name the plan's `**TDD:**` line prescribes literally and the one `ct-step controls` greps for, so the control and the guidance cannot both be satisfied and it stays out of the findings.
